claims.text: Adolescents are particularly worried about schooling during the COVID-19 crisis.
Adolescents are particularly worried about peer relationships during the COVID-19 crisis.
COVID-19 stress is associated with increased loneliness in adolescents.
COVID-19 stress is associated with increased depression in adolescents.
The positive relationship between COVID-19 stress and loneliness/depression is stronger for adolescents who spend more time on social media.
More time spent connecting virtually to friends during the pandemic is associated with greater depression beyond COVID-19 stress.
Spending more time with family during the pandemic is associated with less depression beyond COVID-19 stress.
Spending more time on schoolwork during the pandemic is associated with less depression beyond COVID-19 stress.
Time spent with family during the pandemic is associated with lower loneliness beyond COVID-19 stress.
Time spent connecting to friends during the pandemic is associated with lower loneliness beyond COVID-19 stress.
Engaging in physical activity during the pandemic is associated with lower loneliness beyond COVID-19 stress.

evidence.description: Results showed that adolescents are very concerned about the COVID-19 crisis and are particularly worried about schooling...
Results showed that adolescents are... particularly worried about schooling and peer relationships.
COVID-19 stress was related to more loneliness...
COVID-19 stress was related to... more depression...
...especially for adolescents who spend more time on social media.
Beyond COVID-19 stress, more time connecting to friends virtually during the pandemic was related to greater depression...
...but family time... was related to less depression.
...and schoolwork was related to less depression.
Results show promising avenues to stave off loneliness, as time with family... were related to lower loneliness, beyond COVID-19 stress.
...time connecting to friends... were related to lower loneliness, beyond COVID-19 stress.
...as well as physical activity were related to lower loneliness, beyond COVID-19 stress.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional Online Survey
methodologies.description: Canadian adolescents completed online surveys measuring COVID-19 stress, loneliness, depression, and time spent in various activities during initial pandemic lockdowns.
